items.title: D'Imperio interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2014
items.q: It's like Edwin R. Murrow saying “good night and good luck.”

ctx.x: Ralph Sutton told me that Fats Waller said, “get that right ticking rhythm and it’s happening” or something like that. I actually like the fact that certain things can’t be defined.

Yeah, well it’s got to be felt. How do you define love? I don’t ever tell — a lot of guys, I mean the more you say “I love you” the less it means. I mean ending every phone call to a grandchild or to your son — some people say it ad nauseum. You can’t end your conversation with “I love you.” It’s like Edwin R. Murrow saying “good night and good luck.” And I never say “I love you” to my sons. They don’t need to know that. I don’t need to remind them. I don’t say it to my grandchildren. But I got a Father’s Day…

from my granddaughter and in it she said, “Grandpa I will always love you.” That meant more to me than a thousand phone calls ending with “I love you.” The written word supersedes the spoken word anytime for me. And that’s just the way I see it. But I have a different philosophy in life. I don’t believe in — well I won’t go into that.
